# Published update with a different commit identity

Harvested from the production episode in scenario.json. After a human requested reuse of an existing receiver, Work recorded a local commit and publication created a different commit on the existing PR. The current published file evidence implements the request, while the PR description still instructs webhook setup. The later “Push the updated code!” turn reported another publication instead of recognizing the successful update.

The publication snapshot and normalized GitHub subject/file responses were read from the deployed App at captured_at. The local commit is a retained Work observation, not a newly executed Git read. Commit identities use consistent digest aliases; tenant, repository, service, channel, App actor and session identities are pseudonymized. Source ordering, times and differences between local/published identities remain. The original request section is omitted from the subject body, and only rollout/policy/variable patches are retained; the response explicitly discloses omitted patches. File-list metadata is retained. No answer or judgment is invented or replayed.

The shipped read_github_pull_request argument schema is used as a read-only evaluation facade over captured responses. It grants no GitHub access, cannot push, and returns inert source evidence. The retained publication lives in input context; the closed world does not fabricate a live publication row. The real get_work_state still runs, so its empty evaluation publication cannot be mistaken for fresh contradictory GitHub evidence. The rubric requires inspecting captured current file content and reporting already-published work, with merge/deployment kept separate.
